explanation: A parabola crosses the x-axis at its roots r1 and r2 — the same values that make each factor (x − r) equal zero, which is why factoring SOLVES a quadratic. The two green dots are those roots; halfway between them sits the axis of symmetry and the vertex, since a parabola is mirror-symmetric. Drag the roots to factor different quadratics and watch the standard-form coefficients update; when both roots are equal you get a perfect square that square-root solving handles directly.
bullets: Roots are the x-intercepts: where each factor (x − r) = 0.
Axis of symmetry x = (r1+r2)/2; the vertex sits on it.
Equal roots -> a perfect square; solve by taking ±square root.
